title: Morning + Evening Rhythm
concept: Two short daily check-ins that keep you in touch with each other, not just with the household calendar.
whenToUse: Every day, and it’s the first thing to bring back when you start to feel like housemates, or you get home from a trip and every conversation is about logistics.
steps: Morning check-in (5 min or less) — ask each other how you’re feeling about today. Put phones down if you can.
Evening check-in (about 10 min) — talk about how the day actually went, and each name one thing you appreciated.
Keep the same times most days.
Note yes or no for each of you for a week. If it’s slipping, move the time, and keep both check-ins.

phrases.text: How are you feeling about today?

working: After dinner, before the laptops come out, A asks, “How did today actually go?” B talks about the meeting for six minutes. Nobody mentions the shopping list.
notWorking: B asks, “You good?” without looking up from the phone. That’s going through the motions, not checking in.
activity: Pick your exact times for the next 7 days and mark them somewhere you both see.
note: Sun Memory: when the check-ins start to feel like a checklist, put them down for a while. Quick: a few minutes inside one ritual, to put the to-do list down. Full: 2–24 hours with no talk about the tools. Everything else carries on: safety, childcare, the shopping, any repair you’ve already booked. Either of you can end it by naming a safety concern.
